title: Secretary of State of Connecticut

context.text: Connecticut's November 3, 2026 sample ballots and CT Mirror's voter guide show Stephanie Thomas (Democratic, also on the Working Families and Independent Party lines) and Peter Lumaj (Republican) for Secretary of the State.
Both major-party primaries for this office were canceled because each candidate was unopposed.

candidates.name: Stephanie Thomas
candidates.ballotNote: Cross-endorsed by the Working Families Party and Independent Party.
candidates.currentRole: Connecticut Secretary of the State (since January 2023)

summary.text: Stephanie Thomas is the incumbent Democratic Secretary of the State, elected in 2022 after one term as a state representative. A former nonprofit adviser and small-business owner from Norwalk, she is the first Black person to hold the office.

background.text: Served one term as state representative for the 143rd House District before her election in 2022.
Won the Democratic convention endorsement in a five-way race and then a two-way primary in 2022.

priorities.text: Election confidence: she said the early-voting and security changes in Senate Bill 298 are "in part, about confidence."
Modernizing election technology, including the new TotalVote voter registration system due to launch in December.

record.text: Announced that Governor Lamont signed Senate Bill 298, under which early voters feed ballots directly into tabulators, with updated recount procedures, stronger safeguards for voter-registration data and expanded authority for the Secretary to resolve disputes.
Condemned false online claims that an innocent New Britain woman was an undocumented immigrant who had registered to vote, saying officials should insist on evidence and verification.
Announced that testing of the new TotalVote centralized voter registration system found about 4,700 voter records needing updated district assignments before its December launch.

candidates.name: Peter Lumaj
candidates.ballotNote: Republican nominee; the Republican primary was canceled.

summary.text: Peter Lumaj is the Republican nominee, a Fairfield real estate investor and former immigration legal adviser born in Albania. He has run unsuccessfully for statewide office four times, twice for U.S. Senate, once for governor and once for Secretary of the State; his only appearance on a November ballot was as the Republican secretary nominee in 2014.

background.text: Born in Albania; former immigration legal adviser and real estate investor in Fairfield.

priorities.text: His campaign site describes his platform as "principled governance, economic prosperity, and constitutional values."

candidates.researchNotes: Detailed priorities and positions could not be found on the campaign site pages that loaded; no record of elected office.
